title: Roulette's Edge Is 5%. So Why Did Tables Keep 19%? #shorts
summary: Double-zero roulette has a 5.26% house edge, but Nevada's roulette tables held 19.00% of the chips bought in 2025, because the same money is bet again and again.
sources: Wizard of Odds, roulette basics: double-zero roulette house edge 1/19 = 5.26% on all bets except the 0-00-1-2-3 bet (7.89%); single zero 1/37 = 2.70%: https://wizardofodds.com/games/roulette/basics/

Nevada Gaming Control Board, December 2025 monthly revenue report, 12-month (calendar 2025) columns: statewide total gaming win $15,798,466K (+1.23%); slots $10,713,837K, win 7.13%; table, counter and card games $5,084,629K, win 14.41%; roulette win 19.00%; Las Vegas Strip total $8,815,212K, slots $4,950,173K (7.83%): https://www.gaming.nv.gov/siteassets/content/about/gaming-revenue/december-2025-monthly-revenue-report.pdf
Wizard of Odds glossary, "hold": "The hold percentage will be much higher than the house edge because players tend to circulate through the same money.": https://wizardofodds.com/gambling/glossary/

scenes.narration: Roulette's house edge is about five percent. Nevada's roulette tables kept nineteen.
That's {19 percent|nineteen percent} of the money players turned into chips, in {2025.|twenty twenty-five.}
The trick isn't better odds. It's the same chips, bet again and again, losing a cut every spin.
That's how five percent becomes nineteen.
